scenarios.expected: Recognized archives expose the specified ordered names, metadata, diagnostics, and decoded bytes.
Embedded names remain bounded, independently represented, and semantically identical after round trip.
Malformed structures are rejected or classified as the specified tolerated noncanonical disposition without unbounded reads.
Unsupported compressed payload encodings fail with a stable unsupported or format outcome before unsafe consumption.
Unsupported encode codecs are rejected before opening sources or publishing destination artifacts.
Stored and mixed-compression inputs encode canonically and decode to the original ordered entries.
Unsafe or colliding entry names are rejected before destination effects and cannot escape the extraction root.
Stored entries encode canonically and decode to the original ordered names and bytes.
Zlib entries round trip through the independent wire validator with exact decoded content.
LZ4-frame entries use the qualified profile and round trip with exact decoded content.
JBSA and the digest-pinned Conformance Oracle cross-decode equivalent semantic content in both applicable directions.
BSA 0x69 uses 24-byte folder records and diagnoses nonzero padding without losing inspectability.
BSA 0x69 automatic, explicit Xbox, and cleared miscellaneous flags match the specified profile behavior.
BSA 0x69 sharing, splitting, and logical ordering publish readable deterministic archive parts.
The thin CLI selects BSA 0x69 explicitly and rejects incompatible codec and family combinations.
LZ4-frame processing remains within admitted heap, native, scratch, and output bounds.
Cancellation is observed before publication and all LZ4 credits and owned resources are released.
Focused Archive Family checkpoints record throughput, memory observations, and derived output size under bound conditions.
Family-specific naming, hashing, flags, compression boundaries, source overlays, sharing, splitting, determinism, and empty or multi-entry interactions match their owning specifications.
Starfield v3 method-3 entries use the qualified level-12 raw-LZ4 profile and round trip exact ordered bytes.
Starfield General emits the canonical extra header and selects v2 without a method or v3 with method 3 solely from the compressed codec.
The thin CLI maps -sf1 stored and zlib to v2 and raw LZ4 to v3 method 3, then cross-decodes the output.
An independent bounded scanner accepts canonical Starfield v2 zlib and v3 raw-LZ4 while requiring exact complete payload consumption.
Bounded stored DDS chunks remain diagnosed noncanonical and mixed stored/compressed chunks reconstruct in serialized order.
One through four independently framed DDS chunks retain contiguous mip ranges and reconstruct canonical envelopes with opaque payload bytes in serialized order.
An independent bounded scanner validates Starfield DDS v2 zlib and v3 method-3 raw-LZ4 chunk headers, payload consumption, and reconstructed DDS bytes.
The thin CLI selects Starfield DDS v2 zlib or v3 method-3 raw-LZ4, rejects stored DDS encoding, and cross-decodes the result.
DDS chunk decoding and reconstruction admit packed, decoded, entry, native, and output bounds before allocation or publication effects.
Raw-LZ4 native capability, size admission, memory credits, invalid input, and stable failure mapping are checked before output effects.
Raw-LZ4 cancellation and callback failures release credits without publishing destination effects.
